Michael Jackson's Love for Diana Ross Continues Even in Death -  July 2, 2009 –                                           
 It may have come as a surprise to some that Diana Ross was mentioned in Michael Jackson's will as a secondary caregiver to his three children, but her inclusion was not unexpected to those who had tracked their longstanding relationship, dating back to Jackson's early childhood. In his will, Jackson specified that if his mother Katherine Jackson, his first choice to become guardian for his three young children, died before he did, then he named Ross to take custody of the kids. Omitted from the will was Jackson's ex-wife, Debbie Rowe, the mother of his two older children.
'Michael was obsessed with Diana Ross, but his mother feared she would corrupt him...'

On 3 July 2009, J Randy Taraborrelli explains the deep friendship Michael Jackson had with Diana Ross
The 18-year-old Michael Jackson was coy when I interviewed him back in 1978 and we got on to the subject of his friends. I asked about teenage actress Tatum O'Neal, with whom he was supposed to be going out. 'She's nice,' he said. 'She's teaching me to drive.' I pressed him further. 'Any other friends?' 'Well, I do have one,' he said. 'A very dear, close friend that I can tell my deepest, darkest secrets to because I know she won't tell anyone else. Her name is ... 'He paused for dramatic effect. 'Miss Diana Ross.' It proved to be quite a friendship, lasting the rest of his lifetime. It emerged earlier this week that in his will, drawn up in 2002, he named the 65-year-old singer as the person he wanted to be the guardian of his children should his mother be unable to care for them. Jackson had a thing about divas. All his life he was drawn to powerful women who seemed self-sufficient. There was Elizabeth Taylor, Jane Fonda, Liza Minnelli, even Jackie Kennedy. But Diana Ross was the first. She was a very important influence on him from the very start of his career.  Indeed, legend has it that Miss Ross - then lead singer in the The Supremes - actually discovered Michael Jackson.  Michael and his brothers in the Jackson Five had already auditioned for the same recording company as Ross and had been signed up when they met her. The Jackson Five were performing at a charity event - the 10-year-old Michael, with his Afro hair, bouncing around in front of his brothers and leading the vocals as usual. He recalled looking out into the audience 'and there was Diana Ross. I almost lost it'. Afterwards, they were introduced to her, looking regal in a white silk gown, her smile almost as overwhelming as the diamonds she wore at her ears and around her neck.  'I just want to tell you how much I enjoyed you guys,' she said. 'I hear we're going to be working together.'  A wide-eyed Michael couldn't believe what he was hearing. 'We are?' he asked. She turned to him. 'And you, you're just so cute.' When she pinched his cheek, he blushed. They next saw her a few months later at her home. All their mouths dropped open as she swept into the room in black satin hot pants and gold hoop earrings - 'like a goddess',
Michael's brother Jermaine recalled .

Michael Jackson's Love for Diana Ross Continues Even in Death -  July 2, 2009 –                                           
 It may have come as a surprise to some that Diana Ross was mentioned in Michael Jackson's will as a secondary caregiver to his three children, but her inclusion was not unexpected to those who had tracked their longstanding relationship, dating back to Jackson's early childhood. In his will, Jackson specified that if his mother Katherine Jackson, his first choice to become guardian for his three young children, died before he did, then he named Ross to take custody of the kids. Omitted from the will was Jackson's ex-wife, Debbie Rowe, the mother of his two older children.
'Michael was obsessed with Diana Ross, but his mother feared she would corrupt him...'

On 3 July 2009, J Randy Taraborrelli explains the deep friendship Michael Jackson had with Diana Ross
The 18-year-old Michael Jackson was coy when I interviewed him back in 1978 and we got on to the subject of his friends. I asked about teenage actress Tatum O'Neal, with whom he was supposed to be going out. 'She's nice,' he said. 'She's teaching me to drive.' I pressed him further. 'Any other friends?' 'Well, I do have one,' he said. 'A very dear, close friend that I can tell my deepest, darkest secrets to because I know she won't tell anyone else. Her name is ... 'He paused for dramatic effect. 'Miss Diana Ross.' It proved to be quite a friendship, lasting the rest of his lifetime. It emerged earlier this week that in his will, drawn up in 2002, he named the 65-year-old singer as the person he wanted to be the guardian of his children should his mother be unable to care for them. Jackson had a thing about divas. All his life he was drawn to powerful women who seemed self-sufficient. There was Elizabeth Taylor, Jane Fonda, Liza Minnelli, even Jackie Kennedy. But Diana Ross was the first. She was a very important influence on him from the very start of his career.  Indeed, legend has it that Miss Ross - then lead singer in the The Supremes - actually discovered Michael Jackson.  Michael and his brothers in the Jackson Five had already auditioned for the same recording company as Ross and had been signed up when they met her. The Jackson Five were performing at a charity event - the 10-year-old Michael, with his Afro hair, bouncing around in front of his brothers and leading the vocals as usual. He recalled looking out into the audience 'and there was Diana Ross. I almost lost it'. Afterwards, they were introduced to her, looking regal in a white silk gown, her smile almost as overwhelming as the diamonds she wore at her ears and around her neck.  'I just want to tell you how much I enjoyed you guys,' she said. 'I hear we're going to be working together.'  A wide-eyed Michael couldn't believe what he was hearing. 'We are?' he asked. She turned to him. 'And you, you're just so cute.' When she pinched his cheek, he blushed. They next saw her a few months later at her home. All their mouths dropped open as she swept into the room in black satin hot pants and gold hoop earrings - 'like a goddess',
Michael's brother Jermaine recalled .

Michael disse a Diana Ross: "Eu quero ser como você, Diana".
  Ela disse: "Você apenas seja você mesmo".
O amor de Michael Jackson por Diana Ross continua mesmo na morte - 2 de julho de 2009 -
  Pode ter sido uma surpresa para alguns que Diana Ross tenha sido mencionada no testamento de Michael Jackson como cuidadora secundária de seus três filhos, mas sua inclusão não foi inesperada para aqueles que rastrearam seu relacionamento de longa data, desde a infância de Jackson. Em seu testamento, Jackson especificou que se sua mãe Katherine Jackson, sua primeira escolha para se tornar a guardiã de seus três filhos pequenos, morresse antes dele, então ele nomeou Ross para assumir a custódia das crianças. Omitida do testamento estava a ex-esposa de Jackson, Debbie Rowe, mãe de seus dois filhos mais velhos.

Diana Ross and Michael Jackson first grew close during the filming of The Wiz in 1978. He was 19. She was 33. The 14-year age gap made their relationship taboo for their careers at the time.

According to reports, Michael wanted to marry her. He built a candlelit shrine to her in his home, filled with photos of her. He was reportedly devastated when she married Norwegian businessman Arne Næss Jr. in 1986.

Dirty Diana

After her marriage, Michael released the song Dirty Diana on his Bad album. While he always publicly claimed the song was about groupies, many believe it was written about Diana Ross — a heartbroken and furious response to her marrying another man. 
Diana reportedly had a sense of humor about it, even using the song as introductory music for some of her concerts.

The Will

Perhaps the most telling detail of Michael's love for Diana came after his death. In his will, he named his mother Katherine Jackson as first guardian of his children. His second choice? Diana Ross.

He trusted her more than anyone else with the most precious things in his life — his three children, Prince, Paris, and Blanket.

What He Called Her 
In his 1988 autobiography Moonwalk, Michael wrote about Diana: "She is my mother, sister and lover all combined in one amazing person."

That single sentence captures the complexity of their bond. She was his mentor, his confidante, his inspiration, and the woman he loved.

The Disapproval

Michael's mother, Katherine Jackson, reportedly disapproved of their relationship. She felt Diana was too old for her son. According to some accounts, this disapproval played a role in their engagement ending.

Her Defense of Him 
Even after his death and the controversies that followed, Diana never wavered in her support. In 2019, during the Leaving Neverland fallout, she tweeted: "I believe and trust that Michael Jackson was and is a magnificent incredible force to me and to many others. Stop In The Name Of Love."

The Bottom Line

Diana Ross has kept this secret for decades. Now, at 81, she is finally telling her truth. Their love was real. It was complicated. It was forbidden. But it was also undeniable.

Michael Jackson's Love for Diana Ross Continues Even in Death -  July 2, 2009 –                                           
 It may have come as a surprise to some that Diana Ross was mentioned in Michael Jackson's will as a secondary caregiver to his three children, but her inclusion was not unexpected to those who had tracked their longstanding relationship, dating back to Jackson's early childhood. In his will, Jackson specified that if his mother Katherine Jackson, his first choice to become guardian for his three young children, died before he did, then he named Ross to take custody of the kids. Omitted from the will was Jackson's ex-wife, Debbie Rowe, the mother of his two older children.
'Michael was obsessed with Diana Ross, but his mother feared she would corrupt him...'

On 3 July 2009, J Randy Taraborrelli explains the deep friendship Michael Jackson had with Diana Ross
The 18-year-old Michael Jackson was coy when I interviewed him back in 1978 and we got on to the subject of his friends. I asked about teenage actress Tatum O'Neal, with whom he was supposed to be going out. 'She's nice,' he said. 'She's teaching me to drive.' I pressed him further. 'Any other friends?' 'Well, I do have one,' he said. 'A very dear, close friend that I can tell my deepest, darkest secrets to because I know she won't tell anyone else. Her name is ... 'He paused for dramatic effect. 'Miss Diana Ross.' It proved to be quite a friendship, lasting the rest of his lifetime. It emerged earlier this week that in his will, drawn up in 2002, he named the 65-year-old singer as the person he wanted to be the guardian of his children should his mother be unable to care for them. Jackson had a thing about divas. All his life he was drawn to powerful women who seemed self-sufficient. There was Elizabeth Taylor, Jane Fonda, Liza Minnelli, even Jackie Kennedy. But Diana Ross was the first. She was a very important influence on him from the very start of his career.  Indeed, legend has it that Miss Ross - then lead singer in the The Supremes - actually discovered Michael Jackson.  Michael and his brothers in the Jackson Five had already auditioned for the same recording company as Ross and had been signed up when they met her. The Jackson Five were performing at a charity event - the 10-year-old Michael, with his Afro hair, bouncing around in front of his brothers and leading the vocals as usual. He recalled looking out into the audience 'and there was Diana Ross. I almost lost it'. Afterwards, they were introduced to her, looking regal in a white silk gown, her smile almost as overwhelming as the diamonds she wore at her ears and around her neck.  'I just want to tell you how much I enjoyed you guys,' she said. 'I hear we're going to be working together.'  A wide-eyed Michael couldn't believe what he was hearing. 'We are?' he asked. She turned to him. 'And you, you're just so cute.' When she pinched his cheek, he blushed. They next saw her a few months later at her home. All their mouths dropped open as she swept into the room in black satin hot pants and gold hoop earrings - 'like a goddess',
Michael's brother Jermaine recalled .

snippet.title: Michael was deeply shaken when Diana Ross married Norwegian businessman Arne Naess in 1986.
snippet.description:
He even boycotted the wedding, revealing how much of an emotional role she played in his life.

 The King of Pop met the singer when he was still a child (during the Jackson 5 era), developing a deep relationship that stayed with him throughout his life.

 At the time, the singer was already an established star, with a brilliant solo career following her success with The Supremes. Initially, she was an inspiration to the young Michael, but over time, their relationship evolved into a deep and complex friendship that lasted until the end of his life.

 According to the British newspaper 'Express', Michael Jackson was so obsessed with Diana Ross that he named her as guardian of his children in his will. Biographer J. Randy Taraborrelli, who was a close friend of Michael's, wrote in the book 'Call Her Miss Ross' (1989) about the impact of this relationship: "He idolized me and wanted to sing like me," Ross said of the young Michael.

 In his autobiography 'Moonwalk' (1988), Michael made it clear how important Diana was in his life, describing her as "my mother, my lover and my sister all rolled into one." Despite their intense affection, Taraborrelli claimed they never had a sexual relationship.

The friendship remained strong until Michael's death on June 25, 2009. It was only after his death that information came to light that, in his will, Michael had named Ross as guardian of his children, in case their mother, Katherine Jackson, was unable to perform the role.
